decision.root_cause_hypothesis: The current objective set lacks an explicit within-candidate diversity incentive, so selection favored centrally-located, low-spread designs; this reduced exploration and likely prevented discovering higher-performance regions. (I note mutation_prob=0.0 and random_candidate_ratio=0.0 may also reduce exploration, but the direct objective-level gap is the most actionable first fix.)
decision.rationale: Performance is very low in absolute terms (mean performance = 0.0188 ± 0.0012; best = 0.0192) while population diversity contracted (distance_from_center mean dropped from 0.2667 to 0.2158, Δ = -0.0509, and its std shrank). Adding parameter_spread (registered scorer) will explicitly reward within-candidate parameter variance and complement distance_from_center to recover exploration pressure without changing optimization mechanics.
decision.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Increase within-candidate diversity (parameter std), which should raise population-level diversity measures (distance_from_center mean and std) and expand search into edge regions, improving the chance of finding higher-performance designs in subsequent iterations.
decision.validation_plan_suggested_by_judge: Validator will accept the change only if it yields an improvement over the current accepted state. I expect the next Analyzer to show increased parameter_spread and distance_from_center (mean and/or std) and—over a few iterations—improved performance metrics. If diversity does not recover, consider a follow-up intervention changing optimization_workflow (e.g., set random_candidate_ratio>0 or mutation_prob>0) or adjusting objective weights.

The optimizer appears to be collapsing toward central, low-variance designs. The analyzer recommended adding parameter_spread to directly reward within-candidate diversity; this is a low-risk, focused change that addresses the observed objective-level shortfall without altering core workflow mechanics (mutation_prob and random_candidate_ratio are currently 0.0 and could be changed later if needed).

I will therefore propose adding the registered candidate-wise scorer parameter_spread (maximize) with a moderate weight to restore pressure for within-candidate variability.

decision.root_cause_hypothesis: Optimization population collapse due to no source of new/random candidates (mutation_prob=0.0 and random_candidate_ratio=0.0), causing identical objective values across the evaluated population. If scoring is broken, this change will not restore variance; if generation is the cause, variance should reappear.
decision.rationale: All 32 candidates had identical objective values (performance mean=0.0192 std=0.0000; distance_from_center mean=0.2171 std=0.0000; parameter_spread mean=0.2139 std=0.0000). Current workflow params show no mutation probability (mutation_prob=0.0) and no random injection (random_candidate_ratio=0.0). Injecting random candidates is a minimal, focused change to break duplicate populations and reveal whether the scoring pipeline is functioning.
decision.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Introduce novel, diverse candidate vectors each generation so per-candidate objective variance can reappear. If variance returns, selection pressure and subsequent optimization steps can act to improve performance; if variance remains zero, this strongly implicates a scorer/evaluation bug rather than optimizer collapse.
decision.validation_plan_suggested_by_judge: After the change, check per-objective standard deviations and number of unique candidate vectors. Success is indicated by non-zero std across objectives (variance > 0) and an increase in unique candidates; subsequent iterations should show differentiation and potential improvement in performance beyond the current mean=0.0192.
